newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Index investors stay defensive.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Index investors stay defensive.

text.p: Index options trading remained thin on Thursday but most participants stayed defensive amid concern ahead of Friday's U.S. employment report.
Traders said a smaller than expected weekly jobless claims number on Thursday bolstered talk that the jobs report on Friday would be stronger than expected.
A strong jobs report is likely to fuel fear that the U.S. Federal Reserve will increase interest rates, a move that could hit stock prices, traders said.
But on Thursday, with stock indices slipping moderately in slack trade, options trading was quiet.
One S&P 100 and S&P 500 trader said business had slowed notably after a burst of activity at the opening as the market reacted to the weekly jobless claims figure, which drove bond prices down.
"Even on the OEX it's quiet," he said. OEX options are often more active than SPX options.
At 1210 CDT (1710 GMT) the OEX was off 4.39 at 628.98, just off a fresh session low of 628.87. The SPX was down 4.08 points at 651.53. It had reached an intraday low of 651.46.
The benchmark Dow industrial average was down 27 points at 5,630, near its low for the day.
"People are just on hold ahead of the jobs numbers tomorrow," another index options trader said.
The at-the-money OEX September 630 put was most active, with about 5,300 contracts changing hands. The September 625 put traded 4,250 and the September 610 puts traded 3,775.
On the call side, the September 635 was most active as 3,815 contracts traded. The September 640, 645, 65, 655 and 670 calls all traded well over 1,000 contracts.
Activity was similar in the SPX options, but call volume was particularly slow.
Just two calls, the October 685 and the December 700, had traded more than 1,000 contracts by early afternoon.
Active SPX puts included the November 670, with more than 3,500 contracts traded, the October 625, the October 600 and the September 620, 635, 640, 650, 655, 660 and 670.
